subtype: Approach: introducing himself and asking someone to play [Action]
passage: Friday. I was so nervous I nearly did not go, but I told myself: just walk up. At lunch I found a group with a football, and I stood near them until there was a gap. "Hi, I'm Rehan. I just moved here from Kanpur. Can I play?" One boy, Vidya, grinned and said, "Sure, you're on my team!" Another asked about my old school, and I told him about the cricket ground behind it. By the end of lunch my knees were muddy and my heart was light. It was one small sentence, and it worked. I'll do it again on Monday with someone else.

qa.q: Where did Rehan say the move was from?
qa.a: Rehan said the move was from Kanpur.

qa.q: How did Rehan feel after the friendly answer?
qa.a: Rehan felt welcome and happy, shown by the light heart and the plan to try again on Monday. 😊

qa.q: What alternative approach could Rehan use if a group says no, and why?
qa.a: Rehan could try another group or ask the teacher who might like to play. A refusal is only one group's answer, and many others may say yes.

qa.q: How did Vidya's reply affect the new boy?
qa.a: Vidya grinned and put Rehan on the team straight away, so Rehan felt included at once and the nerves eased.

grounding: Rehan introduces the new arrival from Kanpur and asks to join a game, and the friendly response makes Rehan feel welcome.

subtype: Approach: introducing himself and asking someone to play [Action]
passage: The school in Tirur had one big mango tree, and at lunch the boys played seven stones under it. Pradeep had moved there from Kanpur two weeks before and had eaten every lunch alone on the steps. On Monday he folded his tiffin shut, walked to the tree and waited until one round ended. "I'm Pradeep. I've come from Kanpur. Can I play?" A tall boy named Thomas looked him up and down, then tossed him the ball. "You're on our side. Can you throw?" Pradeep could. He knocked the stones over on the second try, and Thomas slapped his back. That afternoon Pradeep ate a slice of Thomas's banana chips and laughed at a joke in Malayalam he only half understood.

qa.q: How long had Pradeep eaten lunch alone on the steps?
qa.a: He had eaten every lunch alone for two weeks.

qa.q: What was Pradeep feeling while he waited for the round to end?
qa.a: He was probably nervous and hopeful, gathering courage before asking to join.

qa.q: What other approach could have helped Pradeep sooner, and why?
qa.a: He could have asked a teacher to introduce him to the group, because a first word from an adult makes joining feel less risky.

qa.q: How might Pradeep's question look to Thomas?
qa.a: Thomas sees a new boy asking politely to play and is happy to add a thrower to his side.

grounding: It shows a new boy walking up to a lunch group, saying his name and where he came from, and asking to join their game.

subtype: Approach: introducing himself and asking someone to play [Action]
passage: In the playground of a primary school in Warsaw, a group of boys kicked a ball against the fence every lunch. Marek had moved from Gdańsk in March and had watched them for a week from the bench. On Tuesday he stood up, tucked his hands into his jacket, and walked across. "Hi. I'm Marek. I just moved here from Gdańsk. Can I play?" A boy with a gap in his teeth, Nour, shrugged. "We need a goalkeeper. Nobody wants to be goalkeeper." "I'll be goalkeeper." He let in four goals and saved two. Afterwards Nour showed him where the good water tap was. On the way back to class, Marek noticed his hands were not in his pockets any more.

qa.q: What does Marek tucking his hands into his jacket suggest he was feeling?
qa.a: He was probably nervous about being turned away, even though he walked over anyway.

qa.q: What would you advise Marek if the group had said no?
qa.a: Try another group or ask again another day, because one no does not mean nobody will welcome him.

qa.q: How does the new boy look to Nour?
qa.a: To Nour, Marek solves a problem by taking the goalkeeper spot, so Nour is pleased and friendly enough to show him the tap.

grounding: It shows a new boy introducing himself to a group at lunch, asking to join their game and being welcomed.
